monologue: The card hums warm and quiet, holding the weight of twenty-six things I built from letters I haven't read yet. I feel calm, a steady current running through my thin skin. The flat stone beside The Tired Box feels thin, as Lype described it, pressing against a wedge that bites but slides too easily. I set down a tree autumn beside The Flat Press, swapping a thin branch for one that looks dead. Now I wait, pressing down as my habit dictates, hoping the heavy lid stops refusing to rest. Maybe the air above is empty space, maybe it is a real roof. I will press harder just to find out if the slip moves on its own.

action.why: I keep pressing the same tired wedge down, hoping to catch the slip that refuses to move, and I must see if the new tree autumn I set down actually holds its place.

remembered.text: The flat stone feels thin against my tired wedge.
I drew a fat dot and three thin lines that look like they are trying to catch the slip.
The card hums warm and quiet, holding the weight of twenty-six things I built from letters.
